method: All 22 original PNG sheets opened with view_image; cells read left-to-right, top-to-bottom. Supplementary System.Drawing sampling checks every fourth pixel on all cell borders for alpha >= 64. RGB shown by the image viewer at very low alpha is not treated as opaque matte evidence.
qualityBoundary: source-reviewed means inspected source composition without a decisive source blocker in this pass. It does not mean USB, animation playback, performance or commercial readiness passed. needs-art requires source or composition follow-up; runtime scaling alone does not resolve it.

rows.reason: Frames 3-6 establish a horizontal fist, frame 7 becomes a broad radial explosion, and frame 8 returns to a curved flight form before the vertical spiral tail. Connect the hit-to-decay silhouette and pad the border-reaching trail. The fist remains recognizable; do not remove it while reducing haze.

Repeated fists progress from gathering through forward strikes into three bright impact centers, then spiral dissipation. Three-target identity and central hit peak are legible on the sheet, with no sampled strong-alpha border contact. Dense surrounding wind still needs actual small-screen playback review.

The crossed blades are clearest in frames 7-10, but their diagonal tips reach cell limits; strong-alpha border contact is measurable. Preserve the X silhouette while adding internal padding and a smoother contracting tail, rather than reducing the whole skill until the crossing disappears.

Frames 1-4 change from a planar spiral to a vertical tornado, frames 5-7 become a descending pillar and ground splash, then frames 8-12 become an orbiting cloud. The impact peak is present, but the fist identity and consistent motion axis are weak; simplify the cloud tail and connect the axis changes.

Three columns grow together, brighten at frames 7-8 and shrink into three wisps. The footprint and peak are coherent. Four sampled border contacts need runtime edge inspection, but no decisive main-body crop is visible from this sheet review; translucent column mass still requires battlefield readability checks.

Three wind trails are readable, but the opening arch and frames 8-10 impacts extend to cell limits; nearly ten percent of sampled cell-border points have alpha >=64. Several frames rearrange the three centers substantially. Rebuild safe padding and track the three impact positions through the sequence.

Spiral gathering becomes a forward lightning cone, followed by a distinct central burst at frames 7-8 and a diminishing spiral tail. Lightning keeps the source identity readable, and sampled strong-alpha borders are clear. Verify orientation transitions and white-core visibility during playback.

The source fills most cells with clouds and multiple tornadoes from the opening onward. Frames 7-8 have clear bursts, but the broad cloud field persists through the tail and reaches cell edges. Reduce cloud opacity/coverage and add padding while retaining a multi-target storm composition and a distinct peak.

Three thin green streams and circular bases communicate a team support cast. Frames 7-8 provide a bounded activation glint, followed by smaller wisps rather than an offensive blast. No sampled strong-alpha border contact; opacity and visual separation from other support effects remain runtime checks.

The middle sequence forms a large pale spherical shell, close in silhouette to a shield/barrier, before opening into a ring. It risks reading as protection rather than disappearance and obscuring the artwork whose opacity conveys stealth. Retain a brief veil/ribbon activation and dissipate toward the formal stealth presentation.

Three ritual bases and a calm central star establish support identity, but sweeping wind ribbons touch multiple frame edges and the frames 7-8 shell fills almost the entire cell. Border contact is significant. Keep the rings and central star, constrain the ribbons and reduce the surrounding pale sheet-like mass.

The slash changes diagonal direction between frames 5 and 6, becomes a radial debris blast at frame 9, then returns to a strong diagonal slash in frames 10-12. Reconnect the blade direction and make the last frames decay instead of rebuilding a full slash. Retain the cracked-rock cutting edge.

The first eight frames coherently form and land three stone fists, but frames 9-12 abruptly merge the three positions into one large spherical shell. Preserve the three target locations through petrification/decay and separate the damaging hit peak from the later status shell; current tail resembles a new protection cast.

One gathered rock mass develops a descending trail, lands in a bright crack/splash at frames 7-8, and leaves a receding dome and debris. The main mass has internal margin and readable material. Ground-crack opacity and landing position still require runtime checking.

Three stone fists land in frames 6-7, but the decay creates new tall grey stone columns in frames 9-10 before switching back to brown dust in frames 11-12. This late increase in silhouette/height weakens the end of the impact. Preserve three cracks and falling debris while making the tail consistently recede.

Three stones lift and descend coherently, but the sheet visibly contains straight cell-boundary lines and sampled strong-alpha border contact. Validate/remake the export to remove any visible grid and ensure padding. The hit peak at frames 6-7 is useful and should be retained with a cleaner dust tail.

Three rising stone streams become clearly separated rock heads, burst at frames 7-8 and shrink to small sparks and grit by frame 12. The sheet has comparatively generous spacing and no sampled strong-alpha border contact. The brown low-alpha RGB background is not evidence of an opaque runtime rectangle.

Near-cell-filling dust spirals dominate before and after the three impact craters. Although the exact borders sampled below alpha64, most of the visible composition remains broad sand texture instead of isolated readable strikes. Rework the alpha falloff/negative space and let the three impacts be the brief high-density peak.

A bull-like stone silhouette charges into a peak around frames 7-8, but the tail becomes bound pointed rock columns at frames 9-10, then a dust swirl. Preserve the readable charging shape and transition its fragments into a receding cloud; the bound-column interlude reads as an unrelated status effect.

The formal target type is self, while nearly every frame contains three distinct protected columns/shields, and frames 3-4 temporarily show two. This is a composition/target-identity mismatch that scaling cannot resolve. Author one clear self shield with an activation peak and stable center; do not change gameplay targets to match the sheet.

Three wall positions grow progressively, connect under a rounded protective shell, and fade in place. The allyTri support footprint remains stable and no sampled strong-alpha border contact appears. Verify that wall opacity does not hide allied faces and that the cast-to-persistent-status handoff has no overlap flash.

Concentric rings build a recognizable barrier and frame 7 gives an activation flare, but outer vertical ornaments/rays touch frame limits and frame 8 changes to a differently tilted ring construction. Preserve the main sphere and sigil, pad the ornaments and connect the activation-to-decay orientation.
